findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Observed the facility to not have any appropriate sanitizing agent available in-house. The facility was not in operation and will not be cooking for another two weeks, however, an agent should available. There were multiple bleaches available, none are EPA certified. Keila stated that she will have the bleach present before her next cooking event. She is a small batch cook that does not have a store front and is not in operation daily. Keila will send inspector a photo of the bleach to correct violation prior to next operation. Failure to provide documentation of proper bleach by the follow-up date will result in a charge. 




Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods to bare no date. The person in charge (PIC) stated the items were opened (half and half) and prepared (tomato sauce) within the past two days. CORRECTED- the PIC placed the correct dates on the food items. Ensure all TCS items are date marked to be used or discarded within 7 days- the day of preparation counts as day one.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The PIC does not have allergen awareness training. Inspector will email the PIC a website to obtain Allergen training. Obtain training by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspector observed the operator to be preparing red-sauce in the kitchen, but does not have a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM) certificate. Any time food is being prepared a person with a CFM must be present. The owner and operator had a discussion with the Director of Environmental Health, and the operator will be taking the test to receive their CFM at the end of August.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed eggs being stored above butter- which is classified as a ready-to-eat (RTE) food. CORRECTED- The inspector notified the operator and they moved eggs below the butter and other RTE items. Eggs must be stored below RTE foods to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed mop submerged in the basin of the mop bucket in the kitchen. CORRECTED- operator moved mop to the upper portion of the mop bucket to allow for air drying. Mops should be placed in a position to allow for air drying.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]
